text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hizbollah denies Israeli press reports it may have carried out suicide bomb blasts in Jerusalem last week.
- Prime minister Hariri vows to speed up return of displaced.
- Amnesty International says torture is still systematic in Khiam prison in Israel's south Lebanon occupation.
- Syria writes off planned Albright tour, saying the United States was too close to Israel to be taken seriously.

- Interior minister threatens to put down former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili's civil disobedience campaign. Tufaili has launched a "hunger revolt" to pressure the government into easing poverty.
- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad discussed on his visit to Tehran an Arab-Islamic alliance which would include Iran, Syria, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Iraq.
- U.S. ambassador to Lebanon expresses concern over Middle East developments.
